Join us at Entrust
At Entrust, we’re shaping the future of identity centric security solutions. From our comprehensive portfolio of solutions to our flexible, global workplace, we empower careers, foster collaboration, and build solutions that help keep the world moving safely.
Entrust's values are a cornerstone of who we are, our future business growth and how our people grow through it. We model our values by demonstrating that Customer Trust Is Earned, moving with purpose because Speed Is Intentional, taking accountability because We Own the Outcome, and building a collaborative culture where One Entrust Wins Together.
Get to Know Us
Headquartered in Minnesota, Entrust is an industry leader in identity-centric security solutions, serving over 150 countries with cutting-edge, scalable technologies. But our secret weapon? Our people. It’s the curiosity, dedication, and innovation that drive our success and help us anticipate the future.
Help Define the Future of Trust in the Age of AI
The Opportunity
We’re looking for an accomplished Senior Sales & Business Development Executive to help drive the growth of Entrust’s Agentic Trust solution.
As organizations increasingly adopt autonomous and agentic AI, they need new ways to establish identity, authorization, accountability and trust across interactions involving AI agents. This is an opportunity to work at the forefront of that emerging market, helping enterprise customers understand their requirements and translate them into secure, scalable solutions.
You’ll be responsible for developing and closing new business opportunities across an assigned geography or account portfolio, building relationships with senior business and technical stakeholders, and managing complex enterprise sales cycles from initial engagement through to close.
Working closely with account teams, Sales Development, Product, Marketing, Customer Success, technical specialists and partners, you’ll combine market development, consultative selling and enterprise deal leadership to build a strong pipeline and establish Entrust as a trusted partner in the evolving Agentic AI ecosystem.
What You’ll Do
• Become a subject-matter and sales expert for Agentic Trust, bringing relevant industry and competitive insight into customer conversations.
• Build a strong pipeline through targeted prospecting, referrals, events, partners, Sales Development and cross-sell opportunities.
• Develop new enterprise opportunities involving AI agents, identity, delegated authorization, assurance, auditability and governance.
• Create and execute strategic territory and account plans, identifying priority organizations, buying centres, use cases and routes to market.
• Build relationships with executive sponsors, AI leaders, security leaders, technical decision-makers and procurement teams.
• Identify new business, expansion and cross-sell opportunities within designated accounts.
• Own complex opportunities from qualification and discovery through solution alignment, validation, commercial negotiation and close.
• Lead value-based discovery and coordinate demonstrations, workshops, proofs of value and technical validation.
• Use Command of the Message and MEDDPICC principles to develop strong qualification, mutual action plans, decision criteria and close strategies.
• Develop compelling proposals, pricing strategies and commercial plans, and negotiate enterprise agreements in line with company policy.
• Orchestrate internal account teams, technical specialists, Product, Marketing, Customer Success, leadership and partners to move opportunities forward.
• Maintain accurate CRM information covering opportunities, activities, contacts, pipeline and forecasting.
• Provide clear business and forecast updates, proactively identifying deal risks and actions required to close.
• Feed customer insight, competitive intelligence and emerging market requirements back into Product and Marketing.
What We’re Looking For
Basic Qualifications
• 8+ years of successful enterprise technology sales experience, including individual quota responsibility.
• A strong track record of prospecting, building qualified pipeline and closing complex new-business and expansion opportunities.
• Experience managing long, multi-stakeholder enterprise sales cycles involving executive, business, security, technical, legal and procurement audiences.
• Demonstrated ability to develop senior executive relationships, articulate business value and negotiate enterprise agreements.
• Experience collaborating across account teams, Sales Development, pre-sales, Product, Marketing, partners and Customer Success.
• Experience selling enterprise software, cybersecurity, identity, cloud, SaaS, AI or related technology solutions.
• Familiarity with Command of the Message and MEDDPICC sales methodologies.
• Must be able to lawfully work in the country where the position is based, with unrestricted work authorization.
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience selling emerging or category-defining enterprise technology, where educating customers and creating a compelling business case are critical to success.
• Understanding of areas such as agentic AI architectures, non-human identity, delegated authorization, AI governance, Zero Trust or enterprise trust infrastructure.
• Experience selling into regulated industries, including financial services, insurance, government, healthcare or critical infrastructure.
• Bachelor’s degree in Business, Technology, Engineering, Computer Science or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
Why This Role?
This is an opportunity to join Entrust at an important point in the evolution of enterprise AI. Rather than selling into an established category with predetermined buying patterns, you’ll help customers define how trust, identity and governance need to evolve for an agentic world.
You’ll combine strategic business development with complex enterprise selling, working with senior stakeholders to turn emerging AI security and trust challenges into meaningful business outcomes.
If you’re an experienced enterprise technology seller who thrives in developing new markets, creating opportunities and navigating complex buying environments, we’d love to hear from you.

•
Career Growth: Whether you’re a budding developer or a seasoned expert, we’re invested in your professional journey. With learning-forward initiatives and exciting challenges, your growth is our priority.
•
Flexibility: Life is all about balance. Whether you’re remote, hybrid, or on-site, we offer flexible options that fit your lifestyle.
•
Collaboration: Here, your voice matters. Our teams thrive on sharing ideas, brainstorming solutions, and working together to build a better tomorrow.
We believe in securing identities—but it doesn’t stop there. At Entrust, we’re passionate about valuing all…

The Company
Imerys is the world’s leading supplier of mineral-based specialty solutions for the industry with €3.4 billion in revenue and 12,300 employees in 40 countries in 2025. The Group offers high value-added and functional solutions to a wide range of industries and fast-growing markets such as solutions for the energy transition and sustainable construction, as well as natural solutions for consumer goods. Imerys draws on its understanding of applications, technological knowledge, and expertise in material science to deliver solutions which contribute essential properties to customers’ products and their performance. As part of its commitment to responsible development, Imerys promotes environmentally friendly products and processes in addition to supporting its customers in their decarbonization efforts.
Imerys is listed on Euronext Paris (France) with the ticker symbol NK.PA.
The Position
Processing Operative
Job Summary
Processing Operative/ Loading Shovel Driver
Day Shift | Monday to Friday | Newton Abbot
£27,573.14 + £1,918.80 Shift Allowance
Not everyone wants to spend their working week stuck behind a desk.
If you're happiest operating machinery, working as part of a close-knit team, and seeing the results of your efforts at the end of every shift, this could be exactly what you're looking for.
We're looking for a Processing Operative to join our team in Newton Abbot, helping to produce high-quality mineral products used in industries around the world.
This is a hands-on role where safety, teamwork and reliability matter. You'll spend much of your shift operating a loading shovel and production equipment, keeping materials moving efficiently through the process while helping us meet production targets safely and effectively.
The Shift Pattern
• 37.5 hours per week
• Monday to Friday only
• Rotating weekly shifts:
• 6:00am - 2:00pm
• 2:00pm - 10:00pm
• No regular weekend working
What You'll Be Doing
No two shifts are exactly the same, but your responsibilities will include:
• Operating loading shovel and plant equipment safely and efficiently
• Running shredding, blending and milling processes
• Carrying out routine equipment checks and inspections
• Completing pre-start safety checks
• Identifying and reporting equipment defects
• Supporting basic maintenance activities
• Maintaining high housekeeping standards across the site
• Working closely with production and maintenance colleagues
• Helping us achieve production targets without compromising safety or quality
What You'll Bring
• At least 2 years experience of Loading Shovel driving
• A full UK driving licence
• Experience working in an industrial, manufacturing, quarrying or production environment
• Good numerical, written and basic IT skills
• A strong focus on health and safety
• The ability to work independently and as part of a team
• A practical, hands-on approach to problem-solving
Why Join Imerys?
At Imerys, we're proud of the role we play in delivering essential mineral solutions used in everyday products across the globe.
More importantly, we're committed to creating a safe, supportive workplace where people can build long-term careers.
When you join us, you'll benefit from:
• 25 days' holiday plus Bank Holidays
• Generous pension scheme
• Private Medical Insurance
• Life Assurance
•  Income Protection
• Enhanced family-friendly policies
• Cycle to Work scheme
•  Employee Assistance Programme
• Health and wellbeing support, including mental health resources, flu vouchers and eyecare vouchers
• Long-service and recognition awards
•  Paid volunteering leave and carers leave
• Employee discounts portal
•  Sick Pay Scheme
What Good Looks Like
You'll be someone who:
• Takes pride in doing the job properly
• Puts safety first, every time
• Enjoys working with equipment and machinery
• Can be relied upon by colleagues
• Maintains high standards of housekeeping and quality
• Works positively as part of a team
About Imerys
Imerys is the world's leading supplier of mineral-based speciality solutions. Our products and technologies support industries across the globe, helping customers improve performance while reducing environmental impact.
If you're looking for a stable role with a global business, a supportive team, and a genuine opportunity to build a long-term career, we'd love to hear from you.
Apply today and take the next step with Imerys.
Closing date for applications 17th November 2026

Site: The Portland Hospital for Women & Children-London
Full time permanent: Monday to Friday (37.5hrs pw)

•
Foundation Degree in Healthcare Play Specialism - Foundation Degree in Healthcare Play Specialism OR Level 4 Diploma in Specialised Play for Sick Children and Young People

Significant post qualification experience working with children/ young people in a hospital environment

Originally founded over 50 years ago by Dr Thomas Frist, HCA has gone on to become one of the world’s leading healthcare providers. In the UK, we’re one of the largest providers of privately funded healthcare and have invested over £500 million in the latest treatments, technology, techniques, medication and facilities. Being part of a large multisite, established healthcare group we can offer you unrivalled opportunities for career progression through internal and external courses, as well as working conditions that prioritise both your mental and physical wellbeing.
We believe that by caring for our employees, we empower them to provide exceptional care for our patients. That’s why we offer a host of flexible benefits that reflect the invaluable contribution they make every day. As a Senior Play Specialist you would be eligible for:
•
25 days holiday each year (plus bank holidays) increasing with service, with option to buy or sell leave to suit you
•
Private Healthcare Insurance for treatment at our leading hospitals
•
Private pension contribution which increases with length of service
•
Season Ticket Loan and Cycle to Work scheme
•
Group Life Assurance from day one
•
Critical illness cover
•
Enhanced Maternity and Paternity pay
•
Corporate staff discount for all facilities including Maternity packages at The Portland
•
Comprehensive range of flexible health, protection and lifestyle benefits to suit you
•
Discounts with over 800 major retailers
Culture and values
At HCA UK we believe exceptional care starts with our people. We celebrate the unique perspectives and different experiences each of us bring as we know that when you feel seen, heard and supported you can be at your best for our patients, and each other.
Our mission is simple, above all else we’re committed to the care and improvement of human life, a clear statement that extends to both our patients and colleagues. To achieve this, we live and breathe four core values:
•
Unique and Individual: We recognise and value everyone as unique and individual
•
Kindness and compassion: We treat people with kindness and compassion
•
Honesty, integrity and fairness: - We act with absolute honesty, integrity and fairness
•
Loyalty, respect and dignity: We trust and treat one another as valued members of the HCA UK family with loyalty, respect and dignity

bristolmyerssquibb.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com.description_excerpt:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.
Location: Uxbridge - candidate must be based on-site 50% in line with BMS' global hybrid working policy.
Position Purpose
As part of the Real-world Data Research (RWDR) team, you will get the opportunity to work with a collaborative team in an inclusive and supportive environment.
You will be an individual contributor responsible for performing non-interventional research projects in support of key customer groups including medical and health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) and others for International Markets (Europe, APAC and rest of world).
Project work includes identification of appropriate data sources, input into the study design, overseeing programming, analysis and summary of data and collaboration with stakeholders on interpretation and presentation of results.
You will have the opportunity to contribute towards team/department initiatives with goals of optimizing and innovating RWD research.
Key Responsibilities
• Conduct thorough and careful analysis of data, including:
• Overseeing programming of the appropriate statistical analyses (including performing programming).
• Delivering results to customers in appropriate formats.
• Assisting with follow-up questions and interpretation of results.
• Assist with the identification of appropriate data sources for the research objectives, acquiring and storing the data for the project.
• Actively engage with customers on study concept development, protocol and statistical analysis plan (SAP) writing, and dissemination (e.g., abstracts, manuscripts).
• Communicate the results of analyses conducted effectively orally and in writing
• Manage complex work environment, balancing demands from multiple customers to execute projects.
• Make sound scientific decisions based on a balance of data, analysis, and experience
• Work seamlessly in flexible manner across diverse therapeutic areas and assets, study designs and data sources.
Qualifications & Experience
• Advanced degree in a quantitative discipline such as biostatistics, epidemiology or a related field.
• Pharmaceutical and/or Epidemiology/ Outcomes Research experience.
Required Knowledge and Competencies
• Deep understanding of secondary and/or primary patient data sources and demonstrated ability in using such data sources for real-world research and analysis purposes.
• Demonstrated abilities to analyze observational data for pharmaco-epidemiology, outcomes research, and market research.
• Ability to effectively manage research projects.
• Ability to effectively communicate a study’s objectives, methods, and findings.
• Proficient in R programming to execute these studies; ability to program more advanced analytics and use of Github, is a plus.
• Ability to write (or critically review) the scientific content and analytical sections of protocols, statistical analysis plans, final reports and dissemination.
• Demonstrated interest in and working knowledge of AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) to support research activities.
• Ability to apply statistical methods to real-world studies (e.g., survival analysis, logistic/multivariate regression); knowledge on machine learning methods (e.g., clustering, prediction, NLP) is a plus.

Reporting to the Senior Program Manager and with a clear progression path, this role is accountable for the end-to-end delivery of multi-site, Research, Study and New Product Introduction (NPI) projects, ensuring that the project delivers the expected outcomes.

• Change Management
• Reporting & Communication
• Cross Functional Team Management

Essential

Beneficial

Stage 1: Recruiter Review

Stage 3: 60‑minute Behavioural & Competency Interview

IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. The Team:
We are a small, cross-functional team that owns its services end to end, in production. We work closely with product and the business — close enough that “what should this order do next?” is a conversation, not a ticket.
Much of the interesting work lives at the OMS boundary. Because the order flow runs through this service, the OMS describes the business process directly — and that is exactly what makes the role a demanding one, and an unusually influential one.
Your role in the team’s success:
This team owns the Order Management System (OMS), a central part of our trading platform. The OMS controls the order flow for incoming orders: it is where an order’s path through the platform is decided, tracked and recorded.
You will join as a senior engineer on that service: designing and building Java services where correctness is not negotiable and latency is measured rather than guessed. When something goes wrong here, the teams who trade and support our clients feel it straight away.
We are looking for an engineer who wants the domain as much as the engineering. You do not need to arrive as a trading expert, but you do need to want to become one.

• Build and maintain market connectivity: FIX sessions and venue-specific protocols, including certification and conformance testing with counterparties.
• Model and evolve order and execution state: order types, time-in-force, partial fills, amends, cancels, rejects, drop copies, reconciliation and end-of-day processing.

• Apply the same rigour to AI-generated code as to human-written code. You remain accountable for everything that reaches production; in a trading system that accountability is absolute.
• Know when the assistant helps and when it gets in the way and be able to explain and defend every design decision you ship regardless of how the first draft was produced.
• Help the team build good practice: prompting and context patterns, project rules and guardrails, evaluating output, and reviewing critically.
• Contribute to developer experience and automation more broadly — AI-assisted testing, documentation, migrations and support tooling.

• Strong commercial experience building and running production backend systems in Java. This is a Java role on a Java platform; comfort with a recent LTS release (17 / 21 or later) and modern language features is expected.
• Real depth on the JVM: concurrency and the memory model, collections, allocation and garbage collection behaviour, and the ability to profile and measure latency and throughput rather than reason about them by feel.
• Distributed systems fundamentals — messaging, delivery semantics, idempotency, ordering, backpressure, partial failure and recovery — and sound judgement about which guarantees a given problem actually requires.
• Testing you would stake a release on: unit, integration and end-to-end, with an appetite for deterministic or property-based approaches where the domain warrants them.
• Solid SQL and relational data modelling, including schema evolution in a system that cannot lose or misstate an order.
• Comfort with CI/CD, containers, infrastructure as code, and operating what you build: metrics, tracing, structured logging, alerting.
• Clear communication with technical and non-technical audiences alike — you can run a design discussion with dealers in the room.
• Ownership: you take a problem from a vague requirement to monitored, documented, running software.
Strongly preferred — trading domain experience here is what distinguishes a strong candidate for this role from a strong general backend engineer.
• Hands-on experience with an OMS, EMS, PMS or comparable trading system, buy-side or sell-side.
• FIX protocol in production: FIX 4.2 / 4.4 / 5.0 (FIXT), the distinction between session and application layers, custom tags and counterparty dialects, QuickFIX/J or an equivalent (including in-house) engine, and certification with venues, brokers or liquidity providers.
• Other market connectivity: native or binary exchange APIs (ITCH / OUCH and similar), broker and LP APIs, market data feeds, direct market access and order routing.
• Trading domain knowledge: the order lifecycle end to end, order types and time-in-force, execution algorithms, allocations, clearing and settlement, corporate actions, margin and risk, and multi-asset instrument and reference data — equities, futures, options, FX, CFDs.
• Regulatory context and why it shapes design: MiFID II and best execution, transaction and trade reporting, audit trails, surveillance touchpoints.
Strongly preferred — engineering
• Event sourcing and CQRS — having designed, built or run a system along these lines is a real advantage in a service where every state transition matters.

Location:  Home-based, anywhere in the UK, with regular travel to customer sites and periodic visits to our Essex head office

Founded in 1988, Hellenic Systems Ltd builds the systems that run the factory floor. We design and manufacture the hardware that goes with it as well.
We are UK-based and serve over 130 sites across the UK and Europe. Our roots are in food manufacturing, particularly meat and poultry, and we are now extending into any manufacturer with the same problem to solve. A large share of what we ship is built specifically for one customer, which is why our tagline, Built Around You, is meant literally.
Our three software products are CARCASE, our kill line and livestock system, FOPS, our Factory Order Processing System, and FORMIX, our recipe and formulation management system. Our hardware includes weigh scales, touch screen terminals, outer case marking systems, carcass data capture units and label printers.
Since 2023 we have been part of Vesta Software Group, which sits within Jonas Software, an operating group of Constellation Software Inc. Constellation is one of the largest acquirers of vertical market software businesses in the world.
We are also unusually far along with AI for a business our size. It is embedded in how we build software and how we work day to day, not run as a side project, and we expect everyone here to use it.

FORMIX, our recipe and formulation management system, has been rebuilt as a new product and is our main new business push. This role owns the Procure-to-Pay workstream end to end on large-scale Oracle Cloud finance transformation programmes, in front of the client — the full cycle from sourcing and requisitioning through to how suppliers are paid. Finance process context. A clear view of how P2P connects to financial close and controls — accruals, reconciliations, working capital — and to the adjacent finance processes it depends on.

The Principal Solution Consultant - AI drives strategic sales by evangelizing Workiva’s AI capabilities and governed platform. This role supports multiple complex pursuits, demonstrating how customers can leverage AI for regulated reporting through tailored presentations and value-based messaging. You will define Workiva’s strategic position within each organization’s evolving AI and data landscape. This high-impact role requires deep technical expertise and executive presence.
You will engage architects, AI/ML leads, and C-level executives to define Workiva’s role in their AI infrastructure, focusing on data governance, integration, and model orchestration. By positioning Workiva as the system of trust for machine-generated financial, sustainability, and risk data, you will ensure outputs are controlled, reviewed, and defensible. You will partner closely with internal teams—including Sales, Product, and InfoSec—to articulate why a governed core is essential.
What You’ll Do
•
Drive AI Strategy & Mentorship: Lead the AI technical agenda across pursuits, serving as the senior technical voice from engagement through deal closure. Develop reusable IP (patterns, talk tracks, design guidance) and mentor fellow Solution Consultants to elevate AI fluency across the organization.
•
Cross-Functional Discovery & Engagement: Lead technical discovery and alignment across both business functions (Finance, GRC, Sustainability) and IT/Security teams to map customer AI programs, identify where the governed core fits, and ensure safe, compliant integration.
•
Deliver Tailored Demonstrations & Architecture: Prepare high-impact technical demonstrations and produce customer AI reference architectures that clearly show how our API-first platform integrates into their ecosystem to deliver defensible, production-ready outputs.
•
Shape Product Direction: Proactively share field insights with product, engineering, and leadership teams to foster cross-functional alignment and influence the AI roadmap.
•
Represent Workiva in the Market: Engage customers and partners as a public technical voice for Workiva’s AI posture through industry events, thought leadership, and executive briefings.
What You’ll Need
Minimum Qualifications
•
10+ years of technical, customer-facing experience in presales solution consulting, solution architecture, or technical consulting, including a minimum of 3 years focused specifically on enterprise AI architecture
•
Undergraduate degree or equivalent combination of education and experience in a related field
Preferred Qualifications
•
AI Architecture & Technical Depth: Hands-on expertise in modern AI (RAG, agentic systems, MCP, model selection/evaluation) and enterprise data architecture. Ability to write clean code for API interaction and perform technical testing for groundedness and quality.
•
Governance & Security: Understanding of AI governance (NIST, ISO 42001, EU AI Act), security risks (prompt injection, exfiltration), and establishing audit-readiness over machine-generated outputs in regulated environments.
•
Industry & Financial Domain Expertise: Knowledge of corporate reporting (Finance, GRC, Sustainability) and the office of the CFO. Familiarity with source systems like SAP, Oracle, and Snowflake, plus relevant certifications (AWS/Azure/AI).
•
Communication & Strategic Leadership: Proven success articulating architectural visions to C-level executives and representing the company publicly through thought leadership and industry events.
Travel Requirement & Working Conditions
•
Up to 50% travel for customer visits, conferences, and company events
•
Reliable internet access for any period of time, working remotely, not in a Workiva office
Why Join Workiva
Workiva is the platform designed to bring confidence, control, and a competitive edge to the world’s most complex organizations. Our AI-powered platform unifies finance, risk, and sustainability on a single, secure foundation—ensuring data is trusted, traceable, and ready to act on. With an unbroken path from source to output, leaders gain confidence in their numbers, visibility into current and emerging risks, and the ability to move with speed and precision in a constantly changing world.
At Workiva, you’ll bring technology to market that executives, boards, and regulators depend on. The work you do here helps organizations navigate uncertainty, maintain trust, and make decisions that stand up to scrutiny. If you’re energized by meaningful challenges, inspired by collaborative teams, and motivated to help organizations turn uncertainty into advantage, we’d love to meet you.

Elsevier’s mission is to help researchers, clinicians, and life sciences professionals advance discovery and improve health outcomes through trusted content, data, and analytics. As the landscape of science and healthcare evolves, we are pioneering intelligent discovery experiences — from Scopus AI and LeapSpace to ClinicalKey AI, PharmaPendium, and next-generation life sciences platforms. These products leverage retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, and generative AI to make knowledge more discoverable, connected, and actionable across disciplines.
The Search & AI Evaluation team sits within the Platform Data Science organization and is responsible for advancing enterprise-scale search, retrieval, and evaluation capabilities across Elsevier's global products.
About the role
We are looking for a Senior Data Analyst to lead analytics and evaluation efforts for search and retrieval systems. You will own key analytical workflows, define measurement strategies, and generate insights that directly improve ranking quality, relevance, and user experience.
This role is ideal for someone with deep experience in search analytics, experimentation, and data visualization, who can operate with high autonomy and influence decision-making across cross-functional teams.
Key responsibilities
Search Evaluation & Analytics
•
Perform a leading role in analysis of search and retrieval system performance, including ranking quality and relevance.
•
Help define and standardize search evaluation metrics (e.g., NDCG, MAP, recall, precision, CTR).
•
Analyze query behavior, user interaction signals, and content performance to identify optimization opportunities.
•
Conduct deep-dive analyses on ranking performance, query intent, and retrieval gaps.
•
Support evaluation of downstream applications (including GenAI-powered features) where they depend on retrieval quality.
Experimentation & Reporting
•
Help design and lead A/B testing and experimentation frameworks for search and ranking improvements.
•
Partner with product and data science to define success metrics and experiment strategies.
•
Ensure statistical rigor in experiment design, analysis, and interpretation.
•
Build reusable experimentation templates and scalable analysis workflows.
Data Visualization & Communication
•
Own and evolve dashboards and reporting systems tracking search performance and user engagement.
•
Develop clear, actionable data storytelling to communicate insights to technical and business stakeholders.
•
Enable self-service analytics for partners through well-designed reporting tools.
Data Management & Tooling
•
Work with large-scale datasets using modern platforms (e.g., Databricks, Spark, SQL-based systems).
•
Ensure high standards for data quality, metric consistency, and instrumentation reliability.
•
Collaborate with engineering to improve logging, tracking, and observability of search systems.
Cross-functional Impact & Mentorship
•
Act as a key analytics partner to search data scientists, engineers, and product teams.
•

Job Description
Overview
Groundwater modelling sits at the heart of how the UK plans and protects its water supply. Every major abstraction decision, every environmental impact assessment, every investment case for water infrastructure relies on models that are robust enough to inform policy and withstand regulatory scrutiny. The demand for this work is growing- and so is the complexity.
We’re looking for an Associate Groundwater Modeller to join our groundwater resources team within the Water Management Consultancy. This isn’t a delivery-only role. At Associate level, you’ll own a portfolio of projects, lead client relationships, develop new areas of business and shape how the team grows. You’ll still be technically hands-on where it matters, but the balance shifts towards leadership, commercial ownership and building something bigger.
The role is flexible across the UK, with our core groundwater teams based in Birmingham, Epsom, Oxford and Peterborough.
Your role
• Owning and growing a portfolio of groundwater modelling projects- winning, delivering and managing work across our client base of water companies, regulators and major water users.
• Building and maintaining trusted client relationships, understanding their strategic challenges and positioning AtkinsRéalis as their partner of choice for groundwater work.
• Leading complex technical work to a high standard- conceptualisation, data gathering, numerical modelling, interpretation and reporting- while delegating effectively across the team.
• Developing new areas of business for the team, identifying opportunities and shaping proposals that extend our reach into new clients and new problem areas.
• Contributing to the development of innovative approaches and digital tools that strengthen how we deliver groundwater modelling at scale.
• Mentoring and developing junior staff, providing training on modelling approaches and building the team’s capability over time.
• Working across disciplines- collaborating with hydrologists, water resource planners, environmental scientists and digital specialists on projects spanning water supply, strategic planning, resource optimisation and environmental assessment.
• Championing high standards of technical performance and quality across everything the team produces.
About you
• You’re an experienced groundwater modelling specialist who’s ready to step into a role where you own the client relationship, the commercial picture and the team development- not just the technical delivery.
• Degree in science, engineering or mathematics, with a postgraduate qualification in hydrogeology or a related subject. Ideally chartered through a relevant professional body.
• Comprehensive experience building, developing and updating conceptual and numerical groundwater models at regional scale, including model use for assessing abstraction impacts on the environment.
• Ideally experienced with UK regional groundwater models.
• Wider experience across water resources hydrogeology and hydrology- WINEP investigations (low flow, WFD No Deterioration, Environmental Destination, catchment water quality), signal and pumping tests, borehole design, groundwater flooding or water resource planning.

Lloyd’s is the world’s leading insurance and reinsurance marketplace, bringing together the world’s leading risk takers to advance global progress.

How we deliver this, matters. We take the risk, make things happen, and own the outcome — working together across our global network to turn insight into impact.
Lloyd’s is seeking to recruit a Head of Capital Modelling on a FTC (Fixed Contract) for 12 Months to cover a period of maternity leave. You will lead one of the most important components of how we understand risk and capital across the Lloyd’s market. Reporting directly to our Chief Risk Officer, you’ll take responsibility for the Lloyd’s Internal Model (LIM) and lead our market-level capital modelling. You’ll oversee the determination of Lloyd’s regulatory capital requirement and help shape how we manage risk to the Central Fund. You’ll lead the design and development of its next generation, making it simpler and more effective while maintaining the standards expected by Lloyd’s and our regulators.
What you’ll do
You’ll set the direction for capital modelling at Lloyd’s and turn complex analysis into decisions that matter.
You’ll:
• Lead the development, operation and annual update of the Lloyd’s Internal Model.
• Oversee the calculation of Lloyd’s regulatory capital requirement.
• Shape and deliver the next generation of the LIM, aligned to Lloyd’s strategy.
• Lead major model change activity and engagement with the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA).
• Ensure ongoing compliance with UK Solvency II capital requirements.
• Lead analysis of member capitalisation and risks to the Central Fund.
• Bring together Lloyd’s central and market views of capital to identify differences and drive action.
• Connect capital modelling with investment, catastrophe, reserving, finance, risk and market oversight.
• Communicate complex modelling findings clearly to senior stakeholders, regulators and rating agencies.
• Lead, coach and develop the Capital Modelling team, with responsibility for 3 direct and 18 indirect reports.
You’ll also be a member of the Senior Leadership team and Internal Model Oversight Committee, giving you a meaningful voice in the decisions that shape Lloyd’s.
What you’ll bring
You’ll combine deep capital modelling expertise with the judgement and influence to operate confidently at senior level.
We’re looking for:
• Deep technical knowledge of capital modelling.
• Strong understanding of Lloyd’s and the wider London and international insurance markets.
• Broad knowledge across areas such as reserving, reinsurance, exposure management, underwriting and risk.
• Understanding of UK Solvency II requirements and UK GAAP.
• Experience influencing and working with senior stakeholders.
• Evidence of leading significant change.
• Strong analytical, decision-making and problem-solving skills.
• The ability to make complex technical subjects clear and relevant.
• Experience leading, coaching and developing high-performing teams.
• A degree or equivalent experience.
• FIA qualification, or an equivalent recognised actuarial qualification.
Being inclusive at Lloyd’s is integral to how we work — and how we deliver impact.
We aim to build a diverse, inclusive environment that reflects the global markets we serve, where everyone is treated with dignity and respect and supported to reach their full potential.
We take the risk by challenging traditional thinking and being proactive about inclusion. That means being open and positive about workplace adjustments, prioritising health and wellbeing, and investing in diversity and inclusion training so everyone feels able to contribute and succeed.
We make things happen by turning our commitment into action. Through employee networks, mentoring, volunteering opportunities and sustained investment in professional development, we create an environment where inclusion is experienced day‑to‑day — not just talked about.
We own the outcome by focusing on impact. By bringing together diverse perspectives and the best minds in the industry, we work collaboratively with underwriters and brokers to create innovative, responsive solutions that share risk and solve complex problems across global markets.

Position Summary
Why join our team?
We are expanding our team of privacy experts to support the Samsung Electronics’ European Service Business (“ESBO”).
ESBO processes large quantities of Samsung’s first-party data and third-party data to provide consumers with Samsung services on Samsung mobiles and Samsung Smart TVs in Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA). The data is especially relevant to our advertising business, Samsung Ads, where Samsung data is its unique selling proposition.
To manage these risks, Samsung has a global team of privacy experts. They are integral to the continued success of Samsung’s new and existing products.
Given the importance of consumer trust, Samsung is a privacy-forward company. We are focused on making sure that our consumers’ personal data is treated fairly and within the scope of relevant data protection legislation.
We are looking for a Senior Privacy Manager – Consent & Transparency to join our rapidly growing advertising and services business as an integral part of our data privacy and compliance function for EMEA Service Business.
You will lead the privacy side of a new ESBO consent and transparency framework and support the team on general privacy matters across ESBO.
The successful applicant will report into the Director of Privacy – EMEA and will be based in central London. Some travel may be required. You will work in close partnership with the Product team, who owns the product roadmap and delivery of the framework.
Role and Responsibilities
Your key responsibilities
As a Privacy Manager, you will be the business’s expert on consent, transparency and device-level tracking. This role sits outside the legal team but works closely with product teams, engineering, legal and leadership to embed privacy-by-design and default principles into our operations.
You will be responsible for guiding the business on consent and transparency risk and ethical data use, ensuring our products not only comply with GDPR, ePrivacy/PECR and TCF requirements, but also give consumers a real, informed choice that they understand and can change.
The key responsibilities of this role will be to:
•                   Lead the privacy and compliance workstream for a device-level TCF CMP – consent design, purposes and vendor scope, legal QA of consent journeys, and sign-off gates from design through to rollout.
•                   Own ongoing TCF and regulatory compliance for the CMP once live, including CMP registration and validation, Global Vendor List management, vendor onboarding and removal, and monitoring of TCF policy and version changes.
•                   Own our existing consent mechanisms and transparency products, including privacy notices, first-run and in-device disclosures and user preference controls, keeping them accurate as our products and data flows change.
•                   Conduct and document data protection impact assessments and legitimate interest assessments for consent-dependent initiatives, including audience measurement (JIC) participation and programmatic advertising products.
•                   Maintain a market-by-market view of consent and device-storage requirements across EMEA, tracking regulator guidance and national ePrivacy implementations, and translating changes into product requirements.
•                   Work in close partnership with Product & GTM, converting legal and regulatory requirements into clear product specifications, acceptance criteria and release sign-off.
•                   Assist our partnerships and legal colleagues to on-board new clients, service providers, AdTech vendors and data partners in a privacy compliant and efficient manner.
•                   Assist in the creation, implementation and management of business mandates and privacy processes to ensure policy and regulatory compliance, and maintain privacy-related documentation including records of processing, compliance logs and approvals.
•                   Design, develop and assist with the delivery of business-specific training on consent, transparency and TCF for internal stakeholders.
•                   Support the wider privacy programme on ad hoc matters as workload requires, including business requests, new product reviews and data subject rights requests.
•                   Streamline privacy workflows, leveraging automation and AI tools where applicable.
What we need for this role
To be successful, you will possess the following skills and attributes:
·        Deep understanding of GDPR, ePrivacy/PECR and other EMEA privacy laws, with particular depth on consent, transparency, and the rules on storing or accessing information on a user’s device.
·        Working knowledge of the IAB Europe Transparency and Consent Framework (TCF v2.2) – purposes and legal bases, the TC String, the Global Vendor List and CMP validation.
·        Hands-on experience of consent management in practice – implementing, configuring, operating or directly advising on a consent management platform – and a working understanding of how consent signals are captured, stored and passed downstream.
·        Proven track record of successfully managing data protection compliance and implementing privacy-by-design principles across multiple jurisdictions, including data protection impact assessments and legitimate interest assessments.
·        Ability to work credibly with product and engineering teams: turning legal requirements into specifications that can be built, and reviewing what is built against what was agreed.
·        Ability to quickly and accurately assess practical and business risks in a fast-paced environment and the ability to communicate effectively with all levels of the organisation.
·        Demonstrated success in managing multiple high-priority projects simultaneously, coordinating seamlessly across global teams and functions.
·        Exceptional interpersonal skills and an absolute commitment to professionalism and collegiality.
·        Maintain composure under pressure with a positive, solutions-oriented attitude and collaborative spirit.
Additional desirable skills and attributes which are not necessary, but will be helpful to the role:
·        Industry expertise in media, broadcasting, advertising or marketing, combined with privacy knowledge; connected TV or streaming experience is particularly welcome.
·        Experience of privacy issues in programmatic advertising, including OpenRTB, private marketplace deals and device advertising identifiers.
·        Familiarity with audience measurement or joint industry committee schemes, and the privacy questions that come with impression-level data sharing.
·        Certified Information Privacy Professional (CIPP/E) or other recognised privacy/legal certification.
·        Strong interest in technology, with particular enthusiasm for AdTech or complex data ecosystems.

Group/Division
The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards to enable technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. What You'll Do
In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
KLA's Global Products Group (GPG), which is responsible for creating all of KLA's metrology and inspection products, is looking a Mechanical Design Engineer to join the team based in Newport, UK.
Purpose of the role
We are looking for a Mechanical Design Engineer who is hands on, highly motivated, and a team player. The candidate will be engaged during the entire product lifecycle, from prototype to productization, and play a decisive role in the mechanical design and qualification of future KLA products.
The engineer will support the design, building, and qualification of a wide range of KLA equipment front end modules (EFEMs) and integrated components. The candidate will be expected to provide technical solutions for new requirements and sustaining existing product portfolio and create prototypes for design verification though to production release.
Your day to day responsibilities will include:
• Responsible for the complete mechanical design process, including requirements specification, feasibility studies, cost management, and scheduling.
• Collaboration with cross-functional teams to determine design requirements, implement best design practices, and achieve functional product design solution.
• Design mechanical components in CREO Parametric 3D - Pro/E CAD software.
• Conduct or direct CFD and FEA analyses to optimize Semiconductor Equipment airflow requirements, and mechanical design.
• Reduce 3D mechanical designs to 2D drawing and proper application of mechanical tolerancing/GD&T to achieve desired fit and functionality of manufactured parts.
• Collaborate with suppliers to develop components and sub-system assemblies that will expedite product development timeline.
• Work closely with suppliers to ensure parts and assemblies are built per design, and cost and schedule requirements are achieved.
• Participate in entire design/build cycle, including design, 3D CAD modelling, design review presentations, 2D drawing generation, procurement of prototype parts, system integration, and prototype testing.
Minimum Qualifications
• Holds Degree level qualification in Engineering or related subject (or have equivalent level of experience)
• Experience in design using 3D CAD software, ideally Creo.
• Demonstrate ownership of both project level and task level work, comfortable to lead and drive mechanical design projects.
• Candidate will ideally have experience collaborating with cross-functional teams.
• Strong mechanical engineering fundamentals, including design principles, materials selection, and fabrication/machining methods.
• Experience with 2D drafting and tolerance analysis.
• Experience in several of these areas is desirable: CREO Parametric 3D MCAD - Pro/E software, CFD airflow analysis; FEA analysis; Design for manufacture (DFM); Design of welded sheet metal structures and frames; Measurement instrumentation, testing and data acquisition; Programming in Python, C/C++/C# and/or MATLAB.
Occasional domestic and international travel, including to the United States, may be required as part of this role
What we will offer you?
Annual leave starting at 25 days (plus bank holidays), share scheme, contributory pension scheme, cash health plan, cycle to work scheme, global bonus plan, rewards scheme, life assurance.

We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. Algorithms/Hardware Co-Design for Bayesian and Ising Models
Northeastern University London > Computing, Mathematics, Engineering & Natural Sciences

Funded PhD Project (UK or International Students)

●      Bipin Rajendran (Northeastern University London)
●       Darren Hurley-Smith (University of Kent)

Mode of study: Full-time
Northeastern University London
As part of a major investment, Northeastern University London (NU London) offers PhD studentships to support interdisciplinary research across the humanities, social sciences and digital sciences. The current studentship is part-funded by IMEC and is offered for four years and includes funding towards fees, a stipend at UKRI rates, an additional London allowance, and associated costs such as training.
NU London is both a UK university governed by UK higher education regulations, and the European campus of Northeastern University – a large, top-tier research intensive, Boston-based institution. Founded in 1898, Northeastern received $230.7m of external research funding in 2022, and is the recognized leader in experience-driven lifelong learning. It has campuses across the United States and Canada (in Boston; Charlotte, North Carolina; Portland, Maine; Oakland, California; San Francisco; Seattle; Silicon Valley; Arlington, Virginia; the Massachusetts communities of Burlington and Nahant; Toronto and Vancouver). Whilst the PhD will be a UK qualification, students will have the opportunity to engage with and visit the Northeastern University network overseas as part of their London-based doctoral studies, providing a truly unique and highly sought-after dimension to their research training.
The Project
The project aims to develop algorithms and hardware architectures for Bayesian and Ising Models that can leverage the intrinsic stochasticity of emerging magnetic random access memory (MRAM) devices.
Topics will include:
·       Develop robust methodologies for characterising the stochastic behaviour of existing MRAM devices.
·       Establish the link between device-level statistics and probabilistic algorithms.
·       Build theoretical grounding in probabilistic models (Bayesian and Ising) and how they can be optimized considering the natural characteristics of MRAM devices.
·       Use simulation and emulation tools combined with profiling frameworks for energy, latency, and throughput.
·       Benchmark across representative workloads (e.g., TinyML, edge vision, federated learning).

Job Description:
Early Development Asset Lead
Division / Function: Early Development and Innovation
Summary / Purpose of the Position
The Early Development Asset Lead (EDAL) is a scientific and program leadership role within Ipsen's Early Development and Innovation organization, accountable for integrated development strategy and execution for one or more early-stage therapeutic assets from drug candidate nomination through first-in-human clinical trials.
The EDAL leads the Early Development Asset Team (EDT), a cross-functional matrix team spanning clinical, regulatory, CMC, translational, clinical pharmacology, nonclinical safety, and biomarkers, ensuring that each program advances with scientific rigor, strategic clarity, and accountability to portfolio decisions. The EDAL maintains alignment with Therapeutic Area strategy to ensure EDT plans support agreed portfolio priorities, and serves as the scientific champion for assigned programs, articulating project goals, scientific rationale, and clinical line of sight internally and externally. Depending on pipeline needs, the EDAL may represent Early Development in due diligence as the ED lead within a multidisciplinary global team.
Main Responsibilities / Job Expectations
Program Leadership and Strategy
• Leads one or more Early Development Asset Teams.
• Owns integrated program strategy across preclinical, translational, clinical, diagnostic, and regulatory activities.
• Develops and maintains integrated asset strategy, including target product profile, indication strategy, key development options, competitive context, and evidence required for decision-making.
• Ensures Early Development plans deliver against agreed Therapeutic Area strategy and portfolio priorities, with clear evidence-based rationale for stage-gate investment decisions.
Cross-Functional Planning and Execution
• Integrates input from critical functions and research teams to develop plans that balance scientific risk, timelines, cost, and clinical proof-of-concept potential.
• Ensures adequate resources to deliver approved plans, proactively identifies risks, and leads mitigation strategies.
Governance and Decision-Making
• Presents plans, data, risks, options, and recommendations to governance bodies with scientific credibility, while appropriately leveraging functional expertise.
Team Leadership and Communication
• Builds high-functioning teams through clear communication of program vision, roles, responsibilities, and decision-making expectations.
• Maintains a collaborative, inclusive team environment through influence, coaching, and active stakeholder alignment.
Scientific Leadership and External Evaluation
• Serves as the scientific champion for assigned programs, articulating project goals, translational hypotheses, and clinical strategy internally and externally.
• Contributes to due diligence for in-licensing opportunities and, depending on experience and pipeline need, may coordinate findings and present recommendations to governance.
Behaviors and Experience Required
Education and Experience
• PhD, MD, PharmD, or relevant advanced degree with a minimum of 10-15 years of multidisciplinary drug development experience in the pharmaceutical or biotech industry.
• The level offered will be commensurate with scope, independence, and depth of prior early development leadership experience.
Scientific and Development Expertise
• In-depth understanding of oncology required; experience in immuno-oncology and/or ADCs desirable.
• Broad cross-functional drug development knowledge, with experience in more than one functional area, such as nonclinical, translational, regulatory, or clinical development, strongly preferred.
• Expertise in small molecules, biologics, and novel modalities preferred.
• Experience developing and delivering translational strategies, including biomarker and precision medicine approaches in early-phase clinical trials.
• Experience with regulatory filings, including IND/CTA authorship and health authority interactions, required.
• Strong understanding of drug development from discovery through life cycle management.
Leadership and Matrix Impact
• Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional early development teams, with accountability for integrated program strategy and governance-level presentations.
• Proven scientific and leadership performance in a matrix environment, as evidenced by pipeline contributions, publications, and/or patent applications.
• Demonstrated ability to lead decision-making in a multi-regional, diverse matrix environment.
Communication and Stakeholder Management
• Proficient in written and oral English; French or another European language is an advantage.
• Outstanding communication skills, with the ability to present complex program strategies to senior leadership and governance committees with clarity and scientific credibility.
• Ability to build strong relationships with stakeholders across clinical development, clinical operations, translational pharmacology, regulatory, CMC, commercial, medical, and research functions.
• Ability to integrate scientific, regulatory, clinical, and commercial perspectives into balanced, portfolio-aligned program strategies.
Ways of Working
• Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and competing timelines.
• High emotional intelligence, flexibility, and collaborative mindset, with the ability to seek and evaluate diverse viewpoints.

Wherever you join BDO, you’ll have the chance to learn by doing, work with clients and build your career with people around you to support your development.
The opportunity to build your experience, confidence and career without having to do it alone.
Big responsibility. Personal support.

The Financial Ombudsman Service is an independent, not-for-profit organisation that plays a vital role in UK financial services. Every day we help resolve disputes between consumers, or small businesses, and their financial service providers.
The complaints we deal with vary. In this role, you’ll focus on pensions, where complaints can involve detailed financial information, complex calculations and decisions with a significant impact on a customer’s future.
If we believe a customer hasn’t been treated fairly, we’ll ask the business to put things right. If we think the business isn’t at fault, we’ll explain why. The decisions we make have a huge impact: they can be life-changing for individuals, and they provide insights which are useful for financial businesses.
By joining us as an Investigator, you’ll get to the heart of complaints about pensions. You’ll analyse detailed and sometimes conflicting information, identify what’s missing, ask probing questions and reach fair, evidence-based conclusions. Previous pensions experience is an advantage, but it's not a requirement. We'll give you the technical training you need. What matters is that you're curious, comfortable  working through complexity and able to explain your thinking clearly.

As an Investigator new to the role, your journey will start in our Academy, developing the technical knowledge and investigative skills needed to make fair and reasonable decisions. After that, you’ll work as part of a team, supported by an Ombudsman Manager / Operational People Manager, managing your own caseload and prioritising your work.
You’ll be responsible for:
• Investigating complaints about pensions

• Managing your caseload effectively to achieve productivity, quality and timeliness targets
• Managing relationships with consumers, financial businesses and professional representatives, including responding confidently and constructively when your thinking is challenged
• Communicating with empathy and confidence, listening carefully to both sides, asking probing questions and using sound judgement, and
• Communicating your findings clearly, explaining what you think and why through a clear and structured written response
Person specification
You’ll be a self-starter who can prioritise tasks and work well independently. You’ll enjoy digging into detailed information, following evidence, identifying what doesn’t add up and working through problems where the answer may not be immediately obvious. You’ll also have the confidence and people skills to explain and stand behind your decisions.
Your experience could come from financial services, legal or paralegal work, casework, complaints, claims, regulation, compliance, customer services or another role where you have analysed information and reached reasoned conclusions. Previous pensions experience is welcome but not essential, as full training is provided.

• Experience making fair and balanced decisions, explaining your reasoning clearly
• Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain complex information clearly in both written and verbal formats
• Experience supporting customers through challenging or sensitive situations

Neuberger was founded in 1939 to do one thing: deliver compelling investment results for our clients over the long term. • Join a collaborative and entrepreneurial team environment

London | Hertfordshire | Cambridgeshire.

Discover Village Vet
Village Vet is an established veterinary group providing high-quality primary and advanced veterinary care across London, Hertfordshire and Cambridgeshire.
Our network includes small and medium-sized first-opinion practices, larger 24-hour hospitals and access to specialist referral services through London Vet Specialists and the wider Linnaeus network.

Our first-opinion practices offer opportunities to build lasting relationships with clients and their pets, manage a varied caseload and develop your clinical and surgical skills.
Hospital experience and clinical complexity
Our larger hospitals provide opportunities to work in a more extensive clinical environment, with access to advanced diagnostics, experienced colleagues and a wider range of clinical cases.
Develop your clinical interests
Whether you're particularly interested in medicine, surgery, imaging, emergency and critical care or another area of veterinary practice, we want to understand what motivates you. Opportunities to develop clinical interests and pursue further qualifications are encouraged and supported.
Take your next step

We want our people to feel supported, valued and able to do their best work. That's why we invest in creating an environment where clinical development and high standards of patient care go hand in hand.

Ability to collaborate effectively with stakeholders across different functions and organizational levels

hyperiongrp.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/broadb.description_excerpt:
Who are we?
Howden is a global insurance group with employee ownership at its heart. Together, we have pushed the boundaries of insurance. We are united by a shared passion and no-limits mindset, and our strength lies in our ability to collaborate as a powerful international team comprised of 24,000 employees spanning over 56 countries.
People join Howden for many different reasons, but they stay for the same one: our culture. It’s what sets us apart, and the reason our employees have been turning down headhunters for years. Whatever your priorities – work / life balance, career progression, sustainability, volunteering – you’ll find like-minded people driving change at Howden.
About the role
We build the Android and iOS apps that turn an ordinary phone into a motion sensor for insurance telematics. When a driver gets into their car, the app detects it, records the journey in the background, and uploads it for scoring - with no interaction from the user at all.
This is an Android-first role - where you’d spend most of your time - but you’d join the small team that owns both apps end to end: recording engine, trip lifecycle, upload pipeline, and the app the customer actually sees.
What you’d be working on
· Background journey recording. Foreground services, Activity Recognition and geofencing, surviving Doze, App Standby and aggressive OEM power management. The same battle plays out on iOS - CoreLocation region monitoring, significant location change, background modes.
· BLE beacon detection of a device in the customer’s own vehicle.
· Sensor capture and trip assembly. GPS, accelerometer and gyroscope streams written to disk, compiled into a journey, packaged and uploaded reliably.
· Permission integrity. Ensuring required permissions are always granted and the user notified ASAP if not.
· The customer-facing app: dashboard, journey history and maps, mileage, discounts, onboarding and login - Jetpack Compose on Android, SwiftUI/UIKit on iOS.
· Release engineering: white-label builds for more than one brand, and staged rollouts.
What we’re looking for
Essential
· Strong commercial Android experience in Kotlin, with Coroutines and Flow. You’d also help maintain the iOS app, so you’ll need the appetite to work in Swift.
· Real experience of background execution and its failure modes - foreground services, WorkManager, AlarmManager, broadcast receivers, and why they silently stop firing.
· Comfort with the Android runtime permission model, particularly background location.
· Modern Android UI and architecture: Jetpack Compose, structured concurrency with Coroutines and Flow, DI, local persistence, an HTTP client.
· The instinct to write tests for concurrency, not just happy paths. Most of what breaks here is a race, a lifecycle edge, or a restart mid-flight.
· Practical fluency with AI coding agents, and a clear-eyed view of what they’re bad at. We use them regularly, and we want someone who prompts deliberately, knows when to stop and do it by hand, and reviews the output critically.
· Willingness to debug from evidence - device logs, CSV traces, ANR and crash reports - and add relevant and targeted logging to catch a future problem.
Desirable
· Existing iOS experience - Swift, SwiftUI/UIKit, and the CoreLocation-driven background model. You’d pick this up on the job regardless, but knowing it already is a real plus.
· Prior work in telematics, IoT, fitness/activity tracking, or navigation - anything that runs unattended and drains a battery is the closest analogue to what we do.
· BLE and the ways both Bluetooth stacks disappoint you.
· Location and sensor fusion, GPS accuracy, filtering noisy signals.
· Firebase - Crashlytics, Analytics and Remote Config - and using production telemetry to chase down the bugs you can’t reproduce on your own desk.
You don’t need an insurance background.
How we work
Small team, direct ownership. You’d take tickets end to end - investigate, fix, write it up, raise the PR, ensure QA knows what to test, then monitor the release. Be aware that these are long-lived apps: the recording engine has been evolving since 2017, and there are areas of it that nobody fully understands any more.
Occasionally there’s careful archaeology in code you can’t take on trust, and we’d expect you to leave it better documented than you found it.
Testing happens heavily on physical devices, because a simulator cannot tell you what a phone does in a car - in practice that means recording real test journeys on company phones and test accounts, so regular access to a vehicle, as driver or passenger, is useful. We’ll provide a Mac and phones to test with.
What do we offer in return?
A career that you define. At Howden, we value diversity – there is no one Howden type. Instead, we’re looking for individuals who share the same values as us:
•
Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new
•
We support each other in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges
•
We are determined to make a positive difference at work and beyond
Reasonable adjustments
We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations at Howden to ensure that our positions align well with your needs.  Besides the usual adjustments such as software, IT, and office setups, we can also accommodate other changes such as flexible hours* or hybrid working*.
If you're excited by this role but have some doubts about whether it’s the right fit for you, send us your application – if your profile fits the role’s criteria, we will be in touch to assist in helping to get you set up with any reasonable adjustments you may require.
*Not all positions can accommodate changes to working hours or locations. Reach out to your Recruitment Partner if you want to know more.

Title and Summary
Vice President, Controller
Job Title:
Vice President, Controller - Core Payments
The Vice President, Controller - Core Payments reports to the SVP, Assistant Corporate Controller, and serves as the senior controllership leader responsible for the integrity, governance, audit readiness, and financial reporting environment for the business unit, with particular focus on blockchain and digital payments. This role operates as a strategic partner to global and regional finance teams, Treasury, Corporate Controllership, business leadership, and the Global Business Shared Service Organization (GBSC), providing authoritative accounting judgment and driving consistent execution across a complex global operating environment. The position will help establish and mature a best-in-class controllership function for a highly complex, strategically important, and recently acquired Mastercard business, including oversight of relevant legal entity, statutory, regulatory, treasury, and governance considerations.
Roles and Responsibilities
• Serve as the senior controllership advisor to business and finance leadership, providing accounting judgment on complex transactions, business models, digital asset and stablecoin-related activities, revenue recognition, balance sheet classification, and evolving regulatory matters.
• Drive consistent application of accounting policies, controls, and reporting practices across global and regional teams, including coordination with Corporate Controllership, Technical Accounting, Regional Controllers, GBSC, Tax, Legal, Treasury, and business partners.
• Own senior-level engagement with external auditors and support statutory, internal, regulatory, and other required audits, including audit documentation, issue resolution, and alignment across relevant controllership and GBSC teams.
• Oversee compliance, governance, and financial integrity for relevant business activities and legal entities, including SOX, Internal Audit, ORM, statutory reporting, local audit requirements, and escalation of potential exposures to senior leadership.
• Define and execute the compliance integration roadmap for the acquired business, including identification of applicable regulatory, statutory, SOX, data/privacy, third-party, and financial reporting obligations; assessment of current-state gaps; alignment to Mastercard policy requirements; and development of remediation plans.
• Establish robust compliance reporting for the integration period, including risk and issue tracking, milestone reporting, evidence retention, control-gap status, audit finding resolution, and clear visibility to senior leadership on items that could impact financial reporting, regulatory compliance, or integration readiness.
• Ensure the acquired company maintains audit-ready documentation throughout integration, including process narratives, control evidence, reconciliations, management review support, policy exception approvals, local statutory and regulatory filing support, and formal attestations required before system migration or reporting process transition.
• Ensure compliant legacy processes are maintained until transition, including identification of changes to business activities or regulatory obligations, support for timely data and evidence requests, participation in control walkthroughs and remediation efforts, and confirmation of readiness for policy, process, system, and organizational handoffs.
• Maintain a legal-entity-level statutory compliance register for the digital payments business, including jurisdictional filing deadlines, audit requirements, financial statement preparation obligations, licensing or regulatory reporting triggers, and local reporting requirements.
• Oversee statutory compliance activities specific to digital payments, stablecoins, crypto assets, settlement, safeguarding, and money movement, including coordination with Legal, Compliance, Treasury, Tax, and Corporate Controllership teams to assess requirements driven by regulated activity, regulatory capital or liquidity obligations, and country-specific financial reporting expectations.
• Own the assessment, documentation, and recurring review of divergent accounting conclusions across US GAAP, IFRS, and applicable local GAAP frameworks, including revenue recognition, gross versus net presentation, digital asset classification and measurement, customer safeguarding obligations, settlement balances, foreign currency, intercompany, tax, and statutory bridge adjustments required to support consolidated and local financial reporting.
• Establish controlled US GAAP-to-local GAAP bridge processes for relevant legal entities, including clear ownership of adjustment preparation and review, linkage to statutory ledgers, reconciliation of intercompany and settlement positions to statutory financial statements, review of material manual journal entries, and retention of support sufficient for external audit, statutory audit, and regulatory inspection.
• Drive periodic reviews to confirm statutory reporting readiness, emerging GAAP or regulatory changes, bridge adjustment complexity, audit dependencies, and remediation status across the acquired company’s digital payments footprint.
• Lead monthly, quarterly, and ad hoc management reporting, including variance analysis, technical position support, executive presentations, and recurring or ad hoc updates to senior management and applicable governance forums.
All About You
The successful candidate will be a strategic, senior-level controller with deep technical accounting expertise, strong leadership judgment, and the ability to operate effectively in a complex, evolving, and highly regulated global environment.
• CPA, CA, or equivalent certification required; bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
• Significant senior controllership, technical accounting, audit, or financial reporting leadership experience in a complex global public-company environment, with strong command of US GAAP and/or IFRS.
• Direct experience with crypto assets and/or fiat-backed stablecoins, including fair value measurement, classification, and disclosure.
• Established credibility as a trusted advisor to senior finance, business, controllership, technical accounting, and audit stakeholders on complex, judgmental, and evolving accounting matters.
• Experience with digital assets, fintech, payments, treasury, settlement,…
